title: Student and External Activation

decisionLog.outcome: Reconstructed 2.4.4 around three connected work packages: student proposition and adoption; external reputation and market activation; and strategic survey performance and reputation optimisation. Year 1 will prove the operating model, prioritising internal proposition work and targeted Graduate Outcomes response-rate optimisation while 2.4.1 builds the graduate premium evidence and content estate. Year 2 scales student adoption and tests targeted external activation; Year 3 embeds the strongest approaches and builds sustained reputation and survey-performance capability. Headline resourcing assumes 0.5 FTE dedicated activation/reputation delivery capacity in 2026/27, rising to 1.0 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29, alongside existing shared King's Edge analytics, project-officer and programme-management capacity and an indicative flexible activation/research envelope of £25,000, £50,000 and £75,000. The precise role design, analytical requirement and business-as-usual destination remain to be validated during proposition review.

Added a programme-controlled Strategic Partnerships, Profile & External Engagement Fund to 2.4.4 as the single accounting home for flexible external-engagement investment deployable across King's Edge. The fund is £25,000 in 2026/27, £35,000 in 2027/28 and £45,000 in 2028/29, with a £45,000 annual recurrent BAU planning liability from 2029/30. It is additional to the existing activation, research and survey-intervention envelopes and must not be double counted against 2.2.2 partnership infrastructure or other package budgets.

decisionLog.forum: King's Edge and Digital Student Experience Hub resource alignment
decisionLog.outcome: Retained the existing 2.4.4 activation/reputation allocation and its King’s Edge accounting profile, but agreed that the eventual post design should be broader than a narrowly dedicated communications role. Organisationally the 2.4.4 allocation should be designed alongside the additional 0.5 FTE content-design/editorial provision funded through 4.1.1, creating a combined King’s Edge / Student Experience communications and content capability of approximately 1.0 FTE in 2026/27 and 1.5 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29. The two funding asks remain separate and auditable: 2.4.4 continues to carry its existing King’s Edge share and 4.1.1 carries the additional Hub share.

Rebased the recommended core case for 2.4.4 while protecting the evidence, survey-optimisation and strategic external-engagement functions. Dedicated activation/reputation delivery remains 0.5 FTE in 2026/27 and is now 0.75 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29 rather than 1.0 FTE. The activation/research/survey-intervention envelopes remain £25,000 in Year 1 and are now £35,000 and £50,000 in Years 2 and 3. The Strategic Partnerships, Profile & External Engagement Fund remains £25,000 / £35,000 / £45,000 with a £45,000 BAU planning liability. Organisational alignment with the separate 4.1.1 0.5 FTE content provision remains, creating approximately 1.0 FTE combined capacity in 2026/27 and 1.25 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29 before other institutional contributions.

Specified the first concrete Graduate Outcomes response-rate campaign test within the existing Year 1 optimisation model: ten short campaign video assets, produced through the 2.4.1 content-production route, combined with paid targeted LinkedIn activity focused on priority graduate cohorts identified through response and outcomes intelligence. The intervention should be evaluated as a test of whether targeted paid social and tailored creative improve response in high-value cohorts rather than treated as a generic communications campaign.
decisionLog.notes: The proposed pre-business-case media/campaign funding is an early release against existing Year 1 2.4.1 production and 2.4.4 activation/survey-intervention envelopes. Asset production remains accounted for in 2.4.1; paid targeting, campaign operation and evaluation remain accounted for in 2.4.4.

sourceIntegratedNarrative.summary: Builds student understanding and value around the King’s graduate premium, grows external reputation and market traction, and strategically improves performance in high-value outcomes and reputation surveys.
sourceIntegratedNarrative.detailSummary:
2.4.4 is the activation and reputation layer of the King’s graduate premium. It takes the evidence, narratives and publication-ready assets created through 2.4.1 and ensures they are understood, used and turned into recognised value by the audiences that matter. Its remit is deliberately broader than communications: it combines proposition management, student engagement, reputation building, market activation and strategic survey-performance work.

The deliverable is organised around three connected work packages. WP1, Student Proposition and Adoption, develops a clear King’s Edge and graduate premium proposition for current students and the staff who shape their experience, then embeds that proposition through the student journey. WP2, External Reputation and Market Activation, uses evidence-backed assets and external validation to build profile, credibility and market traction with applicants, families, employers, alumni, partners, international audiences and the wider sector. WP3, Strategic Survey Performance and Reputation Optimisation, treats high-value surveys as strategic performance environments in which King’s can intervene deliberately. Its immediate priority is Graduate Outcomes response-rate optimisation, particularly where positive destination evidence is strong but response is weaker than it should be; it also develops targeted strategies for reputation and employability surveys such as the Global Employability University Ranking and Survey (GEURS).

The three work packages operate as a feedback loop. Survey and reputation intelligence helps identify where recognition or response performance is weak; student and external activation provide targeted interventions; and subsequent performance helps King’s refine the proposition, audiences and activity. 2.4.4 does not recreate the evidence and rich-media production owned by 2.4.1. It consumes those assets and turns them into engagement, recognition, reputation and measurable performance.
sourceIntegratedNarrative.problemSolved: King’s creates significant graduate value, but that value is not yet consistently recognised by students, articulated by staff, visible to external audiences or translated into the survey and reputation performance that shapes institutional outcomes and market position.
sourceIntegratedNarrative.whatChanges: King’s establishes a coordinated graduate premium activation and reputation function that builds student adoption, grows external recognition and market traction, and systematically improves performance in strategically important outcomes and reputation surveys.

caseForChange.problem: The graduate premium only creates strategic value if people recognise it, believe it and use it. At present, student understanding of the wider King’s proposition is uneven, staff-facing language and activation are fragmented, and external communication can struggle to connect robust evidence with a distinctive and repeated account of graduate value. At the same time, strategically important surveys are often treated primarily as reporting exercises rather than environments in which performance can be understood and deliberately improved. In Graduate Outcomes, this can mean strong positive destinations are under-represented where response rates are weak. In external employability and reputation surveys, King’s may not fully convert the strength of its graduates, partnerships and institutional activity into recognition among the audiences whose perceptions shape the result.
caseForChange.opportunity: King’s can manage graduate premium recognition as a connected internal, external and performance challenge. A strong student proposition can help current students recognise and articulate the value they are building. Evidence-backed external activation can turn the growing 2.4.1 asset estate into market and reputation traction. Strategic survey optimisation can identify the mechanics, audiences and interventions that most influence high-value measures, beginning with targeted Graduate Outcomes response-rate improvement and extending to priority employability and reputation surveys. Taken together, these create a closed loop in which evidence shapes activation, activation shapes recognition and measured response shapes the next round of activity.
caseForChange.whyNow: The enabling conditions for a more deliberate approach are coming together during the mobilisation period. 2.1.1 is strengthening course-owned graduate futures evidence, 2.4.1 is beginning to create reusable evidence and content assets, and 2.4.2 will add external validation and future-facing insight. King’s also now has richer Graduate Outcomes intelligence that can support much more targeted response-rate intervention. With the value of higher education, graduate outcomes and employability reputation under sustained scrutiny, there is a timely opportunity to move from dispersed communications and survey activity to an intentional proposition, reputation and performance model.
caseForChange.intendedChange: Across three mobilisation years, King’s moves from fragmented activation to a repeatable model for creating recognised graduate value. Year 1 proves the student proposition and survey-optimisation approach while establishing external audience priorities and testing early messages. Year 2 scales student adoption and uses the expanding 2.4.1 asset base to test targeted external activation while industrialising the strongest Graduate Outcomes interventions. Year 3 embeds the proposition through normal student-facing activity, scales the external reputation approaches that work and establishes an annual strategic survey-performance cycle. By the end of mobilisation, King’s has a clearer route for turning evidence of graduate value into student recognition, external reputation and measurable institutional performance.
